topic: The five-dollar habit: how compound interest works
title: The $5-a-Day Habit That Can Grow Past $180,000 (Compound Interest, Explained)
description:
A one-minute look at how a small daily habit becomes real money through compound interest, and why starting early matters more than starting big.

All returns shown are hypothetical (7% per year, monthly compounding) and are not guaranteed.
This video is for education only and isn't financial advice.

scenes.heading: The five-dollar habit
scenes.narration: Meet Max. Like a lot of Americans, he figures investing is something you do later, once you're rich. But here's a secret worth knowing.

scenes.heading: Small money, every day
scenes.narration: Say Max sets aside just five dollars a day. That's about a hundred and fifty dollars a month. Skip a couple of takeout lunches, and he's there.

scenes.heading: Let it grow
scenes.narration: Now he invests it, at a hypothetical seven percent a year. After ten years, he has about twenty-six thousand dollars. After thirty? *Over a hundred and eighty thousand.*

scenes.heading: Where it came from
scenes.narration: Penny, how much of that did Max actually put in? Just fifty-four thousand. The rest is growth, earning more growth.

scenes.heading: The catch
scenes.narration: The catch? Time does the heavy lifting. Wait ten years to start, and the same habit only reaches about seventy-eight thousand.

scenes.heading: Your move
scenes.narration: So start small, and start today. This video is for education only and isn't financial advice.
